methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective review of 293 unresectable/recurrent pancreatic cancer patients undergoing comprehensive genomic profiling (Dec 2019 to Apr 2023), with follow-up censored on Apr 30, 2024 and a clear definition of TMB-high (>= 10 mut/Mb) assigned by an expert panel. The primary descriptive analyses (prevalence of TMB-high/MSI-H and mutation frequencies) are appropriate for the dataset, but treatment-efficacy inference is limited because only 13 patients were TMB-high and only 6 received pembrolizumab without a comparator group. Statistical methods are basic and suitable (Fisher’s exact, Mann–Whitney U, Kaplan–Meier/log-rank for PFS on pembrolizumab), yet the very small treated sample limits precision and subgroup claims. Heterogeneity in CGP assay type and treatment history is acknowledged but not controllable in this design.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is primarily a retrospective case series focused on the rare TMB-high subset (n = 13) and outcomes in the pembrolizumab-treated subgroup (n = 6), which aligns best with Oxford LoE 4. It is directly clinically relevant because it characterizes TMB-high/MSI-H frequencies in advanced pancreatic cancer and reports real-world pembrolizumab activity (including objective response and disease control rates, and PFS differences between MSI-H plus TMB-high vs MSS plus TMB-high cases). The manuscript also reports actionable germline findings (e.g., BRCA2, MLH1, MSH6) identified via CGP workflows and molecular tumor board review. Clinical impact is constrained by the small numbers and the absence of a control arm.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is appropriate for this retrospective observational study, and the manuscript describes the patient cohort, time window, CGP assays used (tissue and liquid biopsy options), expert-panel review process, TMB-high threshold, and the statistical tests applied. Results are organized into prevalence, clinico-genetic characteristics, and pembrolizumab outcomes, with tables enumerating baseline characteristics and treated-case details and a KM figure for pembrolizumab PFS by MSI/TMB subgroup. The normalized text does not describe public deposition of patient-level data or analytic code, which is common for single-institution retrospective series and limits reproducibility. Key limitations (small sample, treatment heterogeneity, lack of TMB-high vs TMB-low outcome comparison) are explicitly acknowledged.

novelty_literature.justification: The study provides additional real-world detail on a rare clinical subset (TMB-high pancreatic cancer) and reports pembrolizumab outcomes stratified by MSI status, alongside mutation patterns including frequent KRAS/TP53/CDKN2A/SMAD4 alterations and occasional germline findings. Similar questions have been addressed using large genomic databases, but this work adds single-center clinical context (assay mix, tissue sources, and treatment-course details) that those datasets often lack. The conceptual novelty is moderate because it does not introduce a new biomarker threshold or treatment strategy, but it extends evidence in an underrepresented tumor type. Overall it is an incremental, useful contribution rather than a definitive efficacy study.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with methods that map to the results sections (cohort description, genomic profiling workflow, and pembrolizumab outcome analysis). Key quantitative findings are stated in the abstract (TMB-high frequency, MSI-H frequency, response metrics, and median PFS by subgroup) and expanded in the results with referenced tables and figures. Limitations are discussed candidly, including the small number of treated cases and variability in prior therapies. Overall clarity is good and supports cautious interpretation.

key_strengths: Clearly defined single-center cohort (n = 293) with explicit CGP workflow and a prespecified TMB-high threshold (>= 10 mut/Mb) assigned by an expert panel.
Provides real-world pembrolizumab outcomes in a rare subgroup (6 treated TMB-high cases) and separates MSI-H plus TMB-high from MSS plus TMB-high patterns.
Reports clinically meaningful genomic context, including frequent driver alterations and identification of germline mutations via review processes.
key_concerns: Efficacy conclusions are limited by extremely small treated sample size (n = 6) and lack of a comparator group or adjustment for treatment-line heterogeneity.
Outcome reporting is centered on PFS during pembrolizumab; broader endpoints (e.g., overall survival) and systematic response-assessment detail are not prominent in the normalized text.
Data/code are not publicly available in the manuscript, limiting reproducibility and secondary analyses.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a well-reported, clinically relevant retrospective series that adds useful real-world evidence for a rare biomarker-defined pancreatic cancer subgroup, but small numbers and noncomparative design limit it to a solid Tier 3 contribution.
